objective: Classify the 34 three-place knots as delta-matroids, check coverability in the sense of Kazda, Kolmogorov and Rolinek, and show that hub-free networks of knots with pinned and open distinctions are edge constraint problems over coverable delta-matroids, hence polynomial given their theorem, while a hub is the non-delta-matroid all-equal relation on three places, which makes the problem NP-complete for every knot outside the Schaefer classes given Feder's theorem; for the symmetric knots give the general factor version (Cornuejols, Lovasz).
status: Proved by NATIVE-HARDNESS-20261024-001A-P001 (V1 census with standard-library check; complexity corollaries conditional on cited external theorems). All 34 knots are coverable delta-matroids (two even, the parity knots), as are all 155 nonempty three-place delta-matroids; the hub relation all-equal is not a delta-matroid (degree set {0, 3}). Hub-free networks are edge problems over these relations and hubs are all-equal constraints, so given Kazda-Kolmogorov-Rolinek, Feder, Schaefer, Lovasz and Cornuejols, hub-free networks of every knot are polynomial while hubs make the 16 non-Schaefer knots NP-complete: hardness lives in hubs.
title: Hubs carry hardness
